newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Lyonnais reorganises Euro bond trade.
newsitem.headline: Cr Lyonnais reorganises Euro bond trade.

text.p: French bank Credit Lyonnais said on Monday it was reorganising its European government bond trading operations to focus on activities with the best potential in light of the planned 1999 launch of the euro.
The trading and sale of government bonds, previously shared between Paris and London, will be concentrated in Paris to "achieve an improved synergy with the euro", the bank said in a statement.
German Bund and Italian BTP trading activities are to be transferred to Paris from London, while the Scandinavian government bond trading desk in London is to close, a banking source said.

The bank gave no figures on the number of posts affected but the German, Italian and Scandinavian government bond trading desks were believed to employ a total of four people. Four bonds sales posts in London were also expected to be cut, the source said.

The bank said it would emphasize the trading and sales of structured products. The London and Paris teams will be strengthened to improve the products of securitisation, asset swaps and package products based on derivatives already in place, it said.

In addition, Credit Lyonnais is developing its bond activities in the emerging markets of Asia, Latin America, Eastern Europe, Middle East and Africa by reinforcing teams in New York, Hong Kong and London, it said.
